correctness.rationale: Direct polar differentiation yields the linear doubled-phase radius equation. Positivity and exponential contraction of its Green-kernel solution hold for every real epsilon; bounded positive v makes original time complete and proves uniqueness and global attraction. Physical T and the one-turn Floquet factor follow exactly. Tonelli and the elementary Laplace transform of sin^(2n) yield the absolutely convergent positive area series; the single t=pi saddle with I0 asymptotic gives the verified 1/B prefactor. The decoded standalone check.py numerically matches independent graph quadratures and series at positive and noncontracting anisotropies. Finite samples are not the infinite proof.

The complete explicit monotone Bessel law and sharp exponential asymptotic demonstrate arbitrarily large cycle geometry at fixed physical period and fixed stability, across the loss of homogeneous pointwise contraction.
